How Morris County, Texas, Conducts Tax Sales

Morris County, Texas, conducts tax sales to address unpaid property taxes and provide opportunities for buyers to acquire properties. The process is structured to ensure transparency and fairness for all participants. Here’s a detailed guide to the process.

Schedule of Sales

Tax sales in Morris County typically occur on the first Tuesday of the month, starting at 10:00 AM. Auctions are held at designated locations, often near the Morris County Courthouse. To stay informed, check the Morris County Appraisal District’s website for up-to-date schedules and information.

Check out our Auction Calendar for scheduled auctions.

Notification and Public Notices

Public notices are issued ahead of each tax sale to provide essential details to property owners and potential bidders.

Notices include the date, time, and location of the auction. Properties listed for auction are described, including their minimum bid amounts.

These notices are published on the Morris County Appraisal District’s website and in local publications for wider visibility.

Registration Requirements

To participate in a tax sale, bidders must complete the registration process, which includes:

  • Providing valid identification to verify eligibility.

  • Filling out required forms as instructed by the Morris County Tax Office.

  • Confirming that there are no delinquent taxes owed in Morris County.

Complete registration well in advance to avoid delays on auction day.

Preparing for the Auction

Preparation is crucial for success at a tax sale. Prospective buyers should:

  1. Review public notices to identify properties of interest.
  2. Investigate property details, including location, size, and condition.
  3. Check for any liens, encumbrances, or unresolved title issues.
  4. Visit the properties, if possible, to assess their condition and surroundings.
  5. Consult with legal or real estate professionals to address potential liabilities.

Auction Day Process

On the day of the auction, participants should arrive early to ensure they are ready when the event begins. The process includes:

  • The auctioneer starts bidding at the minimum amount, selling properties to the highest bidder.

  • Successful bidders must make payment immediately. Accepted payment methods include cash or cashier’s checks.

  • The event begins with auction rules and updates, so attendees must pay close attention

Post-Auction Procedures

Winning bidders must follow several steps to finalize their purchase:

  1. Record the deed with the Morris County Clerk’s office to establish legal ownership.
  2. Address any outstanding legal or title issues, such as liens or encumbrances.
  3. Ensure timely payment of property taxes to avoid future penalties or complications.
  4. Buyers purchase properties “as-is” and take full responsibility for understanding all associated risks and liabilities.

Redemption Period

Texas law provides a redemption period for former property owners, depending on the property type:

  • Homestead and agricultural properties have a two-year redemption period.

  • Other properties have a 180-day redemption period.

The redemption process requires the former owner to pay the purchase price, recording fees, any taxes paid by the buyer, and a premium. This premium is 25% in the first year and increases to 50% in the second year for eligible properties.
